content: NIPA1, or Non-imprinted in Prader-Willi/Angelman syndrome region protein 1, is a protein in humans encoded by the NIPA1 gene. This gene is responsible for producing a potential transmembrane protein that may function as either a receptor or a transporter molecule, with a possible role as a magnesium transporter. The protein is believed to be involved in the development and maintenance of the nervous system. Although alternative splice variants of this gene have been identified, their biological significance remains undetermined. Mutations in the NIPA1 gene have been linked to the human genetic disorder autosomal dominant spastic paraplegia 6. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of NIPA1. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Nipa1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at generating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers. Male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of gene deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, but no significant abnormalities were observed.
